text:
Alice: Heads up — after yesterday's RBAC refactor a couple of users from org-beta were able to list KMS keys in org-alpha. Repro below, reproduces reliably in staging. Anyone on call? :eyes:
Ben: Ack. Can you paste the repro + request id? Also which deployment rolled?
Carol: Repro steps:
```
# curl against internal admin endpoint
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer user-token' -H 'X-Org-ID: org-beta' \
  https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/projects/org-alpha/kms/keys
# returns 200 with list of keys for org-alpha
```
This looks like header->scope normalization incorrectly mapping project/org headers when the role is org_admin.
DevSecBot: ALERT: routing-v2:org-header-validation FAILED for request 2026-03-19T22:11:03Z — created ticket SEC-7153 https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-7153 :lock:
Dmitri: Likely cause: middleware in auth-service treats workspace_id as optional for org_admin roles; fallback code queries global key cache and doesn't bind to org. I saw a similar pattern in the scope-refactor PR (#4321).
Eva: Do audit logs show the key list call? Why didn't our regression alert fire?
Carol: Audit snippet:
```
2026-03-19T22:11:03Z INFO audit event=ListKeys principal=user@org-beta principal_id=usr_78 action=list keys target=arn:kms:us-west:org-alpha:key/xxxx result=allowed
```
So the service emitted a normal allow; the problem is the authorizer returned allowed for the wrong org.
Ben: Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback PR #4321 (fast) 2) hotfix auth-service to enforce org binding (slower but targeted) 3) block KMS list endpoint at edge for inter-org requests until patched. Thoughts?
Alice: I'm inclined to rollback the refactor to stop blast radius. I'll take the rollback and smoke test.
Dmitri: While rollback is in progress, add a temporary policy in the authn layer to require that X-Org-ID matches token.org_claims OR deny list the legacy header shape. I can push a rule to envoy filters.
Ben: Also rotate any service tokens that might have elevated svc roles and invalidate auth cache: `POST /admin/auth/cache/invalidate` — do this after rollback.
Eva: For compliance: we need to record the users who accessed cross-org resources and notify affected customers. I'll start a ticket with SOC and legal.
Carol: Filed a repro + logs in SEC-7153, attached trace id trace-0a1b2c. Root cause hypothesis: `normalize_scope()` dropped project scoping when role=="org_admin".
DevSecBot: AUTO: attached recent deploys: runtime-service v2.14.0 -> rolled 2026-03-19T03:05 UTC, PRs: #4321, #4318.
Alice: Plan: rollback PR #4321 now (me), Dmitri to push temporary envoy deny rule (10m), Ben to rotate tokens + invalidate caches (20m), Eva to open customer notifications + compliance log (30m), Carol to run postmortem doc stub. ETA 60m for containment.
Ben: Will also add a unit/regression test on scope normalization + add audit assertion that key list events include org_id in structured payload.
Dmitri: After containment, we should add an e2e test that emits malformed header and ensures authorizer rejects cross-org requests.
Alice: I'll post updates here as we go. :white_check_mark:
